newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vols soften as futures sprint ahead.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vols soften as futures sprint ahead.

text.p: Implied volatility of German Bund options eased back on Thursday as a well-bid underlying futures market headed for the upside.

Traders said comments from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp that the central bank could not ignore the weakness of the German economy have sparked a wave of speculation about future monetary policy moves -- raising hopes of a cut in the 3.00 percent repo rate. "The futures are looking pretty lively. They are being well bid," said one options broker on the LIFFE floor. "And as the future goes up, vols tend to come off."

He said implied vols were a little softer but basically in line with Wednesday's closing levels of around 5.20 percent for February, 5.71 percent for March and 5.65 percent for June. By 1356 GMT, the March Bund future was 47 basis points higher at 101.77, having been up to a day's peak at 101.88 earlier in the session.
Traders said call buying, which has been a feature of the Bund options market for the past few sessions, was evident again on Thursday.
"We seen some good call buying again this morning," said another LIFFE options trader. "One house bought 1,000 lots of March 102.00 calls."
LIFFE screens showed volumes of between 1,000 and 4,000 lots have changed hands in the March 101.00 to 103.00 strike calls, suggesting a view that the Bund future has further to go.
But the trader said business had been seen on both sides of the market, with February 100.00 and 101.00 strike put options bought earlier in the session.
